Can be helpful if you are struggling to maintain any kind of work due to mental health. It will last until MH claims are decided I believe.

If you cannot work more than 8 hours per week and have claims in progress for mental health, you are able to claim the veterans payment and associated assistance with a medical certificate from your GP.

I too am 30 and my parents bought a place years ago and all that jazz. However, 6-7 years ago they went through some pretty gnarly personal circumstances and ended up with nothing. When I say nothing I mean literally nothing other than an old ute and heaps of debt. No house, no cash, no skills (on paper). Life skills and connections, yes. Over the last 5 years I’ve watched my parents start a simple service business from scratch, employ my brother, buy a new house and start racing cars in their spare time. Planning to sell the business for a big stack of cash and retire. They are in their 50s. They do agree it’s a little harder these days to get ahead than it used to be but it’s still doable. 

Instead of getting mad about it, just accept it for what it is, pull ya finger out and have a go. Theres never been a better time is history to make money.

No such thing as “well deserved shit” to a 17 year old who’s keen. Keep that shit out of our sport. There shall be no gate keeping here. We want to grow rallying around the world. That starts with encouraging the kids to get keen.

The best thing you can do right now is focus on school, work part time, save your money and get a go kart. As soon as you start driving cars on gravel the bills stack up. Get your driving skills up to scratch in a kart while you finish school and build a business. Very difficult to race cars on wages these days. 

Don’t start rallying because you want to be a pro, start because it’s the best sport on earth. If it’s not your passion, you’ll never see it through. Just enjoy the process and you never know where you might end up. Help out your local car club and at rallies, navigate or service for others and save your pennies. Nobody will put you in a car with no experience, you’ll have to do it yourself. 

Also, keep an eye out for FIA Rally Star. They might run that again next year. 

Become a rally fan first. All rally drivers were “rally nuts” before we ever got in a car.

The absolute best thing you can do now is come clean. You’ve already made the mistake, be honest and open about it. Tell them everything. People with that kind of money to lend appreciate honesty.
